advances: All closed ambient halfspaces and all actual marks in a three-interval product with changed probabilities. The unweighted original product satisfies the target.

proof:
At base $e\in\{-1,1\}$ and height $x$, each containing cap has its own interval contribution at least $p_e(1-|x|)/2$. Either sign of the own cut extends as $\pm(X-x)+L e(z-e)\ge0$ for sufficiently large finite $L$, excluding every other fiber. The smaller own cut attains the lower bound, so $x=0$ uniquely maximizes endpoint depth.

At the middle center, any through-mark nonvertical cap is, up to reflection of $X$, of the form $X+az\ge0$. Its own fraction is $1/2$, and its endpoint fractions are $F(a)$ and $1-F(a)$, where $F(a)=\min\{1,\max\{0,(1+a)/2\}\}$ ranges over $[0,1]$. The minimum mass is $p_0/2+\min(p_-,p_+)$. The pure-base cuts through zero retain the full own interval and one endpoint and do not improve this. Considering through-mark caps suffices by inward parallel translation. A closed halfspace containing a midpoint contains at least one endpoint, so depth at a midpoint is at least the smaller endpoint depth. The measure is invariant under $X\mapsto-X$, so the middle midpoint attains the middle-fiber maximum. This proves the exact formula; subtracting its middle term from its larger endpoint term gives the positive-part form.

The posterior table is proportional to $(e^{-a-t/2},1,e^{a-t/2})$. Initially the maximal depth is $1/2$. For finite $t>0$, $A_t$ has a continuous Gaussian-mixture density and is nonzero almost surely, so $p_-\ne p_+$. The middle term is then $(1-|p_+-p_-|)/2<1/2$, and both endpoint terms are strictly below $1/2$ by positivity of the other weights. This gives the strict expectation drop. Since $A_t/t\to Z_0$, the Gaussian likelihood ratios against $Z_0$ decay exponentially at every other base. The table tends to a point mass, and the same maximum formula, continuous on the closed simplex of weights, tends to $1/2$. Bounded convergence and the two opposite expectation comparisons exclude both martingale directions.

The displayed finite parameters give $(p_-,p_0,p_+)=(1,16,64)/81$ and the three fiber maxima are $1/162,1/9,32/81$, respectively. The endpoint uniqueness above and the strict inequalities give the asserted winner and its persistence. Under the uniform prior either endpoint center has depth $1/6$, while the original middle center has depth $1/2$. At an endpoint point mass the winning endpoint exceeds the other two fiber maxima by $1/2$; continuity gives strict eventual dominance on the corresponding hidden-base event.
statement:
Use the actual body $[-1,1]\times[-1,1]$, with integer bases $-1,0,1$ and uniform conditional laws on their common interval. For any positive base probabilities $p_-,p_0,p_+$, the global normalized depth is
$$
D_*(p)=\max\{p_-/2,\ p_+/2,\ p_0/2+\min(p_-,p_+)\}.
$$
Equivalently for $R=p_-+p_+$ and $D=p_+-p_-$ it equals $1/2-|D|/2+(R+3|D|-2)_+/4$. For the Gaussian observation process with uniform prior, $\mathbb E D_*(p_t)<1/2=D_*(p(0))$ for every finite $t>0$, but $\mathbb E D_*(p_t)\to1/2$. Thus maximal posterior depth is neither a submartingale nor a supermartingale.

At $t=2\log 2,\ a=\log 8$, the unique deepest posterior mark is $(1,0)$ with posterior depth $32/81>1/4$ and original depth $1/6<1/4$. The strict selection holds on an open interval of $a$ of positive probability at that time. The terminal hidden base is an endpoint with original probability $2/3$, and on that event the endpoint center is eventually the unique posterior winner.
title: Gaussian posterior maximal depth has neither martingale direction
